assignment: Prove the vendored-asset refresh is mechanically cheap and correct: (a) rebuild @barkpark/react from source and confirm the fresh tarball carries PortableDoc/renderPortableDocument AND the #6114 (af4fe3a35) list-item {content:[…]} fix; (b) diff templates/search-starter/public/bp-graph.js vs api/priv/static/assets/bp-graph.js and confirm the delta is exactly the setTheme hunk (D12 snapshot policy); (c) locate the bp-table CSS and settle whether the mobile table fix is SDK-side or template-side.
verdict: PROVEN CHEAP — with TWO traps the MUST-RUN recipe itself walks into. (a) Rebuild+pack is seconds and the fresh tarball carries renderPortableDocument, PortableDoc and the #6114 marker `itemInlines` (2 hits in dist/chunk-WHJFKOPS.mjs); the vendored 07-16 tarball has 0 — yet BOTH package.json read version 1.0.0-preview.1, so the version string is provably NOT a freshness signal (content-hash or `grep itemInlines` is). TRAP 1: `npm pack` (the assigned command) emits `dependencies:{"@barkpark/core":"workspace:^"}` — a spec npm cannot resolve (EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL on a lockfile-less install); `pnpm pack` rewrites it to `^1.0.0-preview.3`, byte-matching what the committed vendored tarball declares. The re-vendor slice MUST use `pnpm pack`. TRAP 2: package-lock.json pins each tarball's sha512 and the deploy runs `npm ci` (DEPLOYING.md:90) — swapping the tarball alone gives EINTEGRITY on a cold cache and, worse, SILENTLY INSTALLS THE OLD BYTES on a warm cache (reproduced: stale paper-surface.css line 223 after a green `npm ci --offline`). `npm install --package-lock-only --offline` does NOT rewrite it either; the working recipe is `rm package-lock.json && npm install` (online), after which a cold-cache `npm ci` installs the fresh bytes. (b) The bp-graph delta is EXACTLY the setTheme hunk: one insertion `3061a3062,3080`, 19 added lines, 0 deleted — and `templates/search-starter/public/bp-graph.js` is byte-identical (md5 b9a3b71…) to `templates/astro-search-starter/public/bp-graph.js`, while `api/priv/static/assets/bp-graph.js` is byte-identical (md5 3d95f57…) to `web/public/bp-graph.js`. Re-vendoring is `cp` into both templates; it serves the Next AND the Astro demo in one move. No CI tripwire compares them (D12 left it as backlog; doc-gates.yml's `templates/**` trigger only makes template PRs RUN doc-gates, it compares nothing). (c) The mobile table fix is SDK-SIDE AND ALREADY FIXED AT SOURCE. There is no overflow-x WRAPPER anywhere — the Phoenix reader puts `display:block; max-width:100%; overflow-x:auto` on the `.bp-table` element itself (api/assets/paper-surface/paper-surface.css:241, landed bbf110e19/#5651, present on origin/main), and tsup copyFile ships that exact file as `dist/paper-surface.css`, which the template already imports (document-detail.tsx:13). The vendored tarball's copy is the pre-fix line 223. Blast radius of the mobile table fix = the re-vendor, ZERO code. Also note: the fresh tarball's export surface is identical to the vendored one (PortableDoc, PortableText, renderPortableDocument, toPlainText, BarkparkImage, imageUrl, BarkparkReference — only the chunk grouping moved) and the template imports only `PortableDoc`, so re-vendoring is non-breaking. Charter D4 ("pinned exact @1.0.0-preview.2" from npm) does not describe reality — both templates use `file:./vendor/*.tgz`.
